title: Sony Music moves to add more than 30,000 copyrighted recordings to its lawsuit against Udio

reading.body:
An AI music generation system was trained on copyrighted recordings without authorization from the rights holders. The system was deployed to generate music from text prompts while these training practices remained in dispute. A technical check of the training data against licensed music would have prevented the unauthorized use.

The failure occurred at model development, where copyrighted works were incorporated into training without securing rights in advance. Universal Music Group, Sony Music, and Warner Music Group all sued over this practice. The reports indicate Sony Music alleged over 30,000 copyrighted recordings were used to train the model, though a judge denied Sony's initial bid to add these to its original case.

It is not established what Udio's intent was, what the full scope of unauthorized training data was, or what remedies the courts will ultimately require beyond the settlement agreements already reached with some labels.

summary:
Universal Music Group has settled a lawsuit against AI music startup Udio by reaching licensing agreements. The dispute involved allegations that Udio used copyrighted music to train its artificial intelligence system, which generates original songs from text prompts. Under the settlement, Udio will launch a new platform next year trained only on authorized and licensed music, allowing users to customize, stream and share their creations. UMG did not disclose the financial terms of the agreement.

The settlement marks the first major music licensing deal Udio has secured with a large record label. UMG had previously sued Udio along with Sony Music and Warner Music Group, claiming the startup improperly used songs like The Temptations' "My Girl" to train its model. Udio's CEO expressed enthusiasm about the partnership and stated that artists can opt into the new platform and receive compensation, though specific details remain undisclosed. Meanwhile, UMG also announced a separate partnership with Stability AI to develop music creation tools for artists and producers.
